newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut to get traffic lights after years of chaos.
newsitem.headline: Beirut to get traffic lights after years of chaos.

text.p: Beirut, which boasts some of the world's most crowded streets and unruly traffic, will install traffic lights in the next weeks for the first time since they were knocked out of operation in the 1975-90 civil war.
Newspapers quoted Beirut provincial governor Nicolas Saba on Thursday as saying 4,000 sets of traffic lights had arrived from Italy and would be installed in the Lebanese capital by the end of April.

Authorities have been waiting for an assured 24-hour electricity supply before setting up a traffic light system. The government announced at the beginning of last year that 24-hour electricity had been restored in the city, but power cuts still occur quite often.
